column1: # Exact 15 current-owner obligations for DistSQL query dispatch and response consumption.

column8: The dependency-closed runtime suite exercises all four direct distsql.go sends through the raw response owner, including nil response, first send error, raw order, runtime subset data, and close; Go failpoint process setup, concrete client transport, and the rest of the Bazel package target remain external.
All seven direct top-level obligations in this source file are retained across the injected raw response runtime and the existing metadata and response decoder authorities.

A built request crosses the injected send boundary as a raw ResponseChannel, QuerySelectResult transfers it once into SelectResponseIter, and the existing lazy DistSqlRecordSet drains two decoded rows before close. Concrete TiKV response production remains external.

The live dispatch preserves the caller-supplied marker that result metadata reports for memory tracking and transfers iterator ownership once. A concrete request-bound memory tracker, byte accounting, and release remain external.
The live dispatch preserves byte-paging and concurrency metadata, while the existing RecordSet consumer proves bounded batches. Adaptive Go chunk growth remains external.
The raw send result has one QuerySelectResult owner, receives exact cop plan IDs plus root plan ID, and transfers once into the live iterator.

Runtime data remains attached to the exact raw subset, then merges through the live iterator under the existing collector and root-plan gates; RPC percentiles and exact Go string formatting remain external.

ANALYZE crosses the raw transport boundary with the internal statistics request-source override and restricted result label; two deliberately non-protobuf subsets return unchanged and in order through next_raw. Concrete session client and the exact 16-byte response fixture remain external.

CHECKSUM crosses the raw transport boundary with the source store and general SQL label; next_raw preserves deliberately non-protobuf bytes, and an independently tracked response proves the single idempotent close owner. Concrete session client and the exact 16-byte fixture remain external.
Rust test isolation replaces package-process setup for the bounded runtime; Go failpoint lifecycle remains external.
The Rust suite has no global failpoint mutation and requires no process-wide cleanup; exact Go TestMain failpoint enable-disable behavior remains external.

The decoding owner retains normal-case channel layouts, scalar chunks, runtime statistics, and lower-level error ordering. TestSelectResultIter and its generated terminal cases remain separately owned by server-distsql-streaming-resultset for their connected lifecycle; temporal/timezone rows and concrete transport remain open.
Preserves nil-collector gating, mismatched summaries, cumulative backoff, exact matching summaries, request-stat gating, and lossless arrival order.
Final and intermediate schemas, encodings, chunks, channel indexes, and invalid index rejection execute; timezone and reserved capacity remain open.
TypeDefault and TypeChunk consume scalar string and integer rows across multiple and empty chunks; timestamp timezone materialization remains open.
